rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract rather than from evidence. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the centre (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m in 0.02 m steps) and placed 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the steering signal is read slightly before the wheels reach the tape. A 12 mm footprint is used so that the 25 mm tape is always covered by at least one or two sensors, which avoids false line-loss events on bends. Wheel track 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m and mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that give a stable yaw inertia and a body width that keeps the off-track limit at about 0.07 m. Controller: sensor weights are antisymmetric and scaled to +/-1 at the outside sensors, so the signal stays within about +/-1. kp = 4 gives a strong but not saturating steering response (about 1400 PWM counts at full deflection). kd = 0.3 damps the overshoot that kp alone would cause on the curves. ki = 0.1 is kept small to avoid integral windup on long bends. base_speed = 1.3 (about 2.6 m/s of commanded speed scale, throttle-limited in practice) aims at the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving margin for the slalom. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning the way it was last steering when the tape is lost. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend tracks, with the main risks being oscillation at high speed on the slalom and a possible line loss on the sharpest bend. The next iteration should reduce base_speed or kd if steering_oscillation is high, and raise kp or base_speed if completion_time is too long.
